chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham, who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying regarding a man who emancipated his slave, and death had presented itself, and that was witnessed for him, and his value was six hundred dirhams, and upon him was a debt of three hundred dirhams, and he did not leave anything apart from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He would be one-sixth free from it. But rather, from it for him were three hundred dirhams, and three hundred dirhams were paid off from it, therefore, for him from the three hundred is a third, and it is a sixth from the total'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on emancipating a slave when the deceased leaves only the slave's value and a debt?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'debt priority' in Shia jurisprudence, where the emancipation of a slave is treated as a financial liability against the estate prior to inheritance distribution. It demonstrates the proportional calculation method where the slave's value (600 dirhams) is offset by the existing debt (300 dirhams), leaving a net value that determines the slave's freedom status relative to the total valuation. This ruling underscores the practical application of estate liquidation in early Islamic legal theory, ensuring creditors and emancipated slaves are compensated before heirs receive their shares.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham who said,

‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding a man who emancipated a slave of his, and death had presented itself, and that was witnessed for him, and his value was of six hundred Dirhams, and upon him was a debt of three hundred Dirhams, and he did not leave anything apart from it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be one-sixth free from it. But rather, from it for him were three hundred Dirhams, and three hundred Dirhams were paid off from it, therefore, for him from the three hundred is a third, and it is a sixth from the total’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal from al-Husayn Aban al-Jahm who has narrated the following: “

This is about the case of a man who frees his slave at the time of his death in front of witnesses. The price of the slave is six hundred dirham, his debt is three hundred dirham and he has no other legacy. I once heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘One-sixth of him is free because he owns from him three hundred and the other three hundred is for the debt. Thus out of three hundred one-third is his which is one-sixth of the total.’”
